A1.justification: Both PDFs present DNAChunker with the same authors and core framework. The complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original downstream benchmark results, biological tokenization analyses and ClinVar mutation experiments, including additional results in Appendix B.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical results and adds BEND and DNALongBench evaluations, controlled ablations, computation measurements, motif analyses and structural-variant experiments.

M1.justification: v4 introduces an inference adaptation for long inputs: overlapping windows, scatter/gather reaggregation and reference/alternate-allele features (Appendix C.4). The core segmenter, mask protection, residual gating and losses remain unchanged. The main-text correction from 8 to 30 Transformer blocks agrees with v3 Appendix A rather than establishing an architecture enlargement.

E1.justification: v3 already evaluates NT, revised NT and Genomic Benchmarks. v4 adds BEND's seven tasks and DNALongBench's five tasks, extending coverage to gene finding, epigenomic profiling, variant effects and long-range prediction. It also adds multispecies pretraining ablations and GIAB structural-variant scenarios.

E2.justification: Existing benchmark comparator sets are retained. v4 adds matched 6-mer/BPE controls and single-nucleotide computation comparisons, plus CNN and Caduceus-PH linear-probing comparisons in Figure 2. The biological tokenization comparison changes from DNABERT-2 BPE to GROVER BPE. These changes substantially broaden direct comparison of tokenization alternatives.

E3.justification: Reported pretraining changes from approximately 35B processed bases with Adam/cosine decay to approximately 52B with AdamW/WSD. Fine-tuning search grids expand, and the NT epoch limit increases from 15 to 20. New protocols include controlled 50M-parameter, 2B-token ablations and frozen-backbone, windowed long-input evaluation. These are documented setting changes; retained scores do not establish that earlier experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v4 adds component-removal and multispecies ablations, computation-versus-length analysis, motif-fragmentation tests and structural-variant robustness. The H3C13–15 gene-track case studies are removed. The existing chromosome analysis is substantially revised to examine annotation-specific chunk maxima and SINE-age groups across chr1–22 and chrX.

E5.justification: Revised-NT captions change mean plus/minus standard error to mean plus/minus standard deviation (v3 Tables 3 and 6; v4 Tables 2 and 10). Three seeds and the full table's numerical uncertainty values are retained. The PDFs neither explain the relabeling nor establish additional runs.

E6.justification: Substantial results are added for the new benchmarks and analyses. For example, v4 Table 5 reports overall MCC 0.390 versus 0.332 without mask protection; Figure 4 reports 1.22 versus 2.47 chunks per motif for DNAChunker and BPE. Existing full NT, Genomic and revised-NT tables retain their numbers. The revised-NT summary MCC is corrected from 0.657 to 0.660, and the original NT win count from 10 to 13.

T1.justification: Appendix D newly defines the region-level statistic m_A as the maximum length of chunks whose centers fall inside an annotated region, underpinning the revised biological analysis. Existing routing, dechunking, loss and mutation-similarity equations are unchanged. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The core learnable-tokenization contribution persists, but the headline performance claim expands to five benchmarks covering long-range and variant-effect tasks. The introduction's contributions now explicitly include preserving functional motifs as single chunks, stability under structural variants and improved long-context computational efficiency.

C2.justification: v4 interprets component ablations as evidence of necessity, multispecies gains as benefits from data diversity, and computation savings as compression offsetting routing overhead. Biological interpretation expands to motif preservation and SINE-age gradients, while the robustness explanation extends beyond small variants. These substantially broaden v3's functional-region granularity and indel-stability explanations.

D1.justification: Appendices B–C substantially expand documentation of repeat weighting, retention targets, ratio-loss weight, precision, GPU/step budget and benchmark-specific heads and inference. v4 also resolves the Transformer-depth inconsistency and clarifies vocabulary padding. Conversely, v3's per-task selected hyperparameter tables and explicit fine-tuning GPU and reverse-complement augmentation disclosures are removed.

R1.justification: v4 adds benchmark, annotation and background references and sharpens the contrast between autoregressive and masked DNA models, while retaining the central positioning around learnable tokenization. The DNAGPT citation changes from Yang et al.'s text-detection work to Zhang et al.'s genomic model. Publication updates to H-Net, PatchDNA and Evo2 represent the same works.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, experimental narrative and conclusion undergo substantial paragraph-level rewriting. Revised-NT evaluation moves from ablations into downstream tasks, and the appendices are reordered and extensively restructured. Method exposition remains largely stable; correspondence, publication-header, acknowledgment and conflict-disclosure text also changes.

P2.justification: The architecture diagram is redrawn, and Figure 1c replaces chromosome distributions with motif-fragmentation summaries. v4 adds long-benchmark, computation and motif charts plus BEND and ablation tables. Gene-track plots disappear, chromosome scatterplots become median/p95 bar panels, and the revised-NT summary separates enhancer and promoter rows.

improvement.justification: v3 supports its architectural choices mainly through benchmark performance and observational tokenization analyses. v4 adds controlled component comparisons, quantitative motif and computation analyses, and broader evaluation with documented long-input handling, substantially strengthening attribution and applicability evidence. Expanded implementation details and corrected summaries also help assessment. Removed per-task hyperparameters and unexplained changes to training settings and uncertainty labels remain reporting weaknesses, but the added controlled evidence provides a substantial net improvement.
